caption:
The Polish voice of Geralt, Jacek Rozenek, lost his ability to speak after a stroke in 2019.
For the new Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, he recorded his lines again, and CD Projekt Red used AI trained on his old Witcher 3 lines to make them sound like his voice from 12 years ago.
He agreed to it. The studio calls it a special case.

Is this a good use of AI voice, or a line games should never cross?

Source: Video Games Chronicle, GamesRadar+ · Photo: CD Projekt Red

site_article.summary: CD Projekt Red worked with the AI voice company Respeecher to adjust the Polish voice of Geralt in the upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past, after actor Jacek Rozenek's voice changed following a 2019 stroke. Rozenek consented, and the studio says it uses AI on performances only with consent.
site_article.seo_title: Witcher 3 Songs of the Past: AI used on Geralt's Polish voice
site_article.seo_description: CD Projekt Red and Respeecher used AI, with actor Jacek Rozenek's consent, to make his new Geralt lines match his voice from before his 2019 stroke.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes. CD Projekt Red used an AI model from Respeecher, trained on Jacek Rozenek's original Witcher 3 recordings, to adjust the new Polish Geralt lines he recorded for Songs of the Past. Rozenek agreed to it, and the English version with Doug Cockle needed no AI changes.

paragraphs.text: CD Projekt Red used artificial intelligence to adjust the Polish voice of Geralt of Rivia in Songs of the Past, the upcoming expansion for The Witcher 3, according to reports published on November 11, 2026, by Video Games Chronicle and GamesRadar+. The voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, suffered a stroke in 2019, and his voice changed as he recovered.

Rozenek is the longtime Polish voice of Geralt. Video Games Chronicle reported that the stroke left Rozenek unable to speak and that he returned to voice acting in 2022 after training for hours a day.

Rozenek recorded the new lines for the expansion himself, in the usual way. The studio then sent the lines he had recorded for the base game of The Witcher 3 to Respeecher, a Ukrainian company that builds AI voice models. Respeecher trained a model on that original performance and used it to retouch the new recordings so they sit closer to the voice players heard in the base game.

According to GamesRadar+, the new lines clashed with the original dialogue without that step. Mikołaj Szwed, a localization producer at CD Projekt Red, said in the interview that the studio delivered to Respeecher all of the lines Rozenek had recorded for The Witcher 3. Respeecher's Dmytry Vasylets described the brief as making the actor's voice sound alive, rich and young, as it did in the original game.

Rozenek said the goal was for the voice to be as close as possible to his voice from 12 years earlier, and he said he has great trust in the people who make the game. Both outlets reported that he consented to the use of AI on his performance. The interview was first published by Game File.
A case the studio calls special

CD Projekt Red says its contracts require consent for any AI work on a performance, and that it turned to AI here only because of Rozenek's health situation. Szwed called it a special case and said he sees it as a way to use AI ethically, with consent, to do something good. The studio has worked with Respeecher before, on a Cyberpunk 2077 character whose actor had died, GamesRadar+ reported.

The English version of Geralt, voiced by Doug Cockle, did not need any AI retouching for the expansion, according to GamesRadar+. Nintendo Life reported that Songs of the Past is due next year, in 2027.

Most arguments about AI voices in games turn on copying a performer without permission. This case is built differently: the actor still performs every line, the model is trained only on his own earlier work for the same character, and he signed off on it. That combination of consent, the same performer and a narrow purpose is likely to be cited as a reference point in future arguments over where AI voice tools belong in game production.

The next test is how players react when Songs of the Past ships in 2027, and whether other studios adopt the same consent based approach for veteran actors whose voices have changed with age or illness.
